utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. For the parties, it's been four weeks that we have not seen each other. We'll resume hearing the case but before we invite the Prosecution to call for further, although very short, examination-in-chief of the witness Dunjic, I have a few matters that I would like to briefly raise with you and I'd first like to go into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On the 13th of July 2007, a motion was filed to add a witness to the Prosecution witness list under Rule 92 bis. The parties are hereby informed that the Chamber has decided the matter although not fully put on paper or fully developed the reasons or details but the parties are hereby informed that the Chamber will grant the addition of this witness to the Prosecution witness list, but under Rule 92 ter, not under Rule 92 bis. Then there was a procedural issue in relation to the way in which the Chamber would receive the testimony of Witnesses 48 and Witness 10. I think the Defence has expressed its objection against hearing this evidence through videolink, prior to a motion being filed asking for videolink. For those reasons, and since the Chamber detected that at least some new elements were in there, the Chamber invites the parties to -- or at least invites the Defence to reply this afternoon, later this afternoon, to the motion for videolink in relation to Witnesses 48 and 10, but not to repeat anything that was already part of the submission made by the Defence earlier. So therefore, mainly to respond on any new element the Defence has identified in what is now a motion for videolink. Is that clear? I am aware that of course it's -- these matters are dealt with in a rather rushed way but that's also a result of a recess. If there is any problem with that, of course I would like to hear from the parties. Then finally I wanted to invite the Prosecution to respond by tomorrow to a motion filed by the Balaj Defence but that's about Mr. Roel Versonnen as a witness, but I do understand meanwhile that a motion has been -- a response has already been prepared and on the basis of my information, I even wonder whether there is still any problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We have notified the Trial Chamber by letter, in e-mail, and we filed a motion response to the same effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you intended to do with that witness. I don't know whether that fully therefore I said I wondered whether it had resolved the matter because I could imagine that it did, but I'm not going to assume anything unless the parties finally consider the matter to be resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't believe that it does resolve the matter. I'll have a brief conversation with Mr. Re at the next break but I believe in this instance, based on the courtesy copy of the motion that I received from the Prosecution, that there is still an issue or two outstanding and we may be requesting ability to file a reply which we will do obviously by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then of course the main concern of the Chamber was that, since the urgency of the matter required quick action, to invite the Prosecution to respond but it has done so already so. Now the same request is now for you, if the matter appears not to be resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then these were the matters I had as urgent matters on my agenda. Is there any other matter that urgently should be raised before we continue to hear the evidence of Professor Dunjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply in relation to timing as far as this witness is concerned and bearing in mind the witnesses scheduled to testify later in the week, as Your Honours will appreciate much of the evidence of this witness has been produced in the form of 92 ter statement and a very substantial volume of exhibits and I think we had indicated to the Trial Chamber at the outset that he was one of those witnesses for whom cross-examination was likely to be fairly extensive. My estimation is that I'm likely to require today and tomorrow in respect of this witness but obviously I will be guided by any indications that the Trial Chamber gives in relation to time. Since the witness who was originally planned to testify for Thursday is no longer to testify for Thursday, I can't at the moment see that, on the face of it, that would place pressure of time on the witnesses who are to testify later this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although there are a lot of procedural matters which the Chamber had in mind to deal with on Thursday as well but at least some room seems to be there due to the rescheduling of the witness originally scheduled for Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: For the Chamber's information, the Defence has discussed the matter of the cross-examination of Professor Dunjic and we once again have attempted to coordinate it in such a fashion that it will go as quickly as possible given the extensive amount of information that exists. And we would not be repeating areas that other counsel covered and may well be in a position that we've been oftentimes before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey I take it you are joining Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I would do if I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you had a microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, I will now join with what Mr. Guy-Smith has said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Then, Mr. Dutertre, are you ready to continue the examination-in-chief of Professor Dunjic? I do understand that you would need 15 minutes. I encourage you -- it was announced 15 minutes. I encourage you to keep it in these time limits in finalising the examination-in-chief of Professor Dunjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Professor Dunjic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Professor Dunjic, I quote from page 6823 of the transcript. That is the transcript of the 5th of July of this year, that you gave a solemn declaration, you said, "I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth." You are still bound when you continue your testimony by that solemn declaration you gave at the 5th of July. Mr. Dutertre will now continue. There will be a brief continuation of the examination-in-chief and then you will be cross-examined by counsel for the Defence. Mr. Dutertre, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Professor. I see that the professor has some personal documents with him on the desk. I'm assuming these are copies of the 92 ter statement, but I would prefer that he use the 92 ter and the annexes to be found to the witness's right-hand side, on the desk shared with Mr. Re. Perhaps we can bring them closer to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you recall that I wanted to show a video. It so happens that this video shows a witness for which the Prosecution has filed a 92 bis motion. I don't believe there has been a decision as of yet. However, if that person were to testify, the problem -- the person has problems as regards his or her safety and therefore, I would like to go into private session in order to view this video, if you agree, regardless of any further decisions you may make in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dutertre, private session would still show the images. No it would not show the images. I hear no objections. Of course, if at a later stage this material could be made public, applications can be made for that. We turn to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: (redacted) She was able to describe it even before she saw the clothes that we showed her, as you saw now on this video. We spoke to her first, asking her to identify items of clothing that this victim might have worn and she gave us those descriptions. We took them to this room that you just saw, to look at all the clothes, and from all the clothes that was -- that were there, she was able to pinpoint this skirt and this blouse that was up there, so she was able to state quite with great certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes. And the body where you had noted this pathology is the body R-17; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to have P680, the 65 ter document 680.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you mean provisionally assigned P exhibits? Or a 680 seems to be in the range of the attachments to P618, but might not be a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there was not a provisional number. It was in an exhibit in the 65 ter list which was numbered 680. It hasn't been admitted as of yet. It hasn't been used as of yet. Could we perhaps view the picture right side up? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Professor, I'm not asking you to identify the individuals that can be seen in this photograph but I would like to ask you if the pathology you described, the spinal column of body R-17, would correspond to the pathology of the woman standing to the left dressed in black, who has -- her two shoulders are at different levels?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is only partially visible here. I don't know either of these two people. The person to the left on our screen dressed in black is -- has a slight stoop, and her left shoulder is a bit lower than the other one, but I have to note here that it's a degenerative disease of the spine and it was actually visible from the side, if you have a different -- if you had a different view you would be able to see that. There was -- she had a hump and she had the vertebra that were all fused together, from the pelvis to the cervical vertebra but you cannot really see that all that well because the photograph -- on this photograph she is facing the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. My last question deals with R-23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have to stay in private session at this moment? Because it was mainly --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I apologise. Yes we can go in open session. I forgot to mention that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar. Would you please, Mr. Dutertre, later indicate what portion could be made public so that we can --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. If you would just turn a little note to Madam Registrar then we'll decide after the break from what moment on the session is public again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: One last question on R 23: On page 93 to 95 of your 92 ter statement you said that it's a man aged between 50 and 60, and that it's the body of Isuf Hoxha and that the clothing was identified by Vendim Hoxha. Could you tell the Court which pieces of clothing enabled Vendim to identify his father's body?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let me have a look. He was able to identify a suit consisting of a jacket and trousers, and a sweater. He was also able to identify a black plastic digital watch that was on the wrist of this person. We had taken it off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any other elements that were recognised?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we carried out identification not only on the basis of clothing but also on the basis of anthropologic and forensic elements that we could find on the body, which means the anthropologically estimated age, gender, height and diseases, if any, so that on the basis of the gender, the age, height and forensic characteristics, coupled with a positive identification of the clothing, we were able to carry out his identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dutertre. Professor Dunjic, you'll now be cross-examined by Defence counsel Mr. Emmerson, counsel for Mr. Haradinaj will start. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I first of all make sure that the witness has available to him a full set of the coloured binders which have been prepared for the purposes of cross-examination? There should be a yellow and a brown binder which have been used before. There should in addition be a green binder of documents, a blue blinder containing photographs and post mortem reports, and a grey binder which will be relevant a little later on. Can I ask first of all please that Professor Dunjic be provided with the brown binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to start, if I may, by asking you some questions about two fully fleshed sets of human remains that are shown in photographs taken on the 8th of September, apparently snagged in the concrete section of the canal. If you could start by looking behind tab 2 in the brown file, I think you may have it there, you will see behind tab 2(A) an extract from the transcript of evidence that you gave to this Tribunal in the Milutinovic case and behind tab B, a black and white copy of the photograph that was shown to you during the course of this testimony. And if you could look back at the transcript with that photograph in mind, you are asked, and this is page 5271 of the Milutinovic transcript at line 22, you were asked to look at those photographs and you were told that they should relate to the time that you were in that location and you were asked, "Is that the canal that we see on the screen?" And then at 5272, line 3, your answer is recorded as follows, I'll just read it slowly into the transcript: "Yes, that's the canal. Those two photographs were taken from the direction of Radonjic Lake and the place where the canal narrows down faces Donji Ratiste and Glodjane. That's the concrete part of the canal. And the second photograph is something that I saw with my own eyes when I was on the location. We see two bodies next to the right-hand edge, depending on where you're looking from, two bodies that were floating and that were later found in the earth-covered part of the canal, because this is the concrete part. Out of the concrete part, there is a waterfall and then follows an earthen part. There were heavy rainfalls at the time and these two bodies and a larger one were found in April." Now, pause there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, a technical issue. It's not a matter of substance. We now have more than 7.000 pages of transcript so that when we refer to a binder, tab 2, several weeks later when we read it we are a little bit lost, we are not absolutely certain which document we are referring to. I have experience in particular with Witness 21. In the end we don't know which document we are referring to. Could we perhaps ask the Defence to give a more precise identification number or give the exhibit number or perhaps give an exhibit number as we go along, so that we all have an exhibit number that we can refer to when we read back the transcript several weeks later, otherwise it gets very complicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson has read the relevant portion of the transcript and has mentioned the transcript pages and the case from which it was taken and from what I see, this is a public session, which I think would be sufficient to identify at a later stage what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the case for this particular document, but in other cases where it's a photograph or other types of documents, it may be more difficult to identify the exact exhibit, the exact document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that if Mr. Emmerson is referring to any document which is already in evidence, and I think these photographs were in evidence, that he would, to the extent possible, also for the hyperlinks mention the exhibit number attached to these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll certainly do that. The transcript is Exhibit number D133 and the photographs which the witness was shown during the course of his testimony are D134. I'll obviously endeavour to make that clear with each document that I deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think for the hyperlink it's always good if you say Exhibit D and then the number. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But for the sake of clarity the index to each of these bundles has in the right-hand column recorded the exhibit number where the document has already been exhibited and that is the position for all of the five files that are to be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to return, please, with you, to that passage of the evidence that you gave in the Milutinovic case and can I say first of all I know that this passage has already been shown to you by the Prosecution and you've been asked some questions about it, and I think one of the points that you raised was that the reference to April must be a mistake. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to explain. At the trial that you mention, that is the trial against Milutinovic, I was asked questions and I was shown these two photographs, and I explained what can be seen on those photographs. However, either it was misinterpreted or mistranslated, but at the time I wasn't engaged for that trial for that purpose, I just said that those were events that are linked to April 1998, that these were photographs of locations of events that occurred in April and we worked on them in September. So I think that is quite clear. It was just an error. These bodies, it says, were seen and photographed in April. No. These were events that took place in April and May, around that canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to press you on that explanation just at the moment, Mr. Dunjic. I've understood you to be saying the reference to April is a mistake. If you could just confine for the moment your answers to that question, that is a mistake; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What I want to ask you about for the moment is the sentence which reads, "And the second photograph is something that I saw with my own eyes when I was on the location." Now, I'm going to just ask you to reconsider that answer. Did you see those two bodies floating in the concrete section of the canal with your own eyes when you were on the location; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that on the first day we arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we perhaps check that the witness has the photograph in front of him? I don't have it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He does have it in front of him. It's behind tab 2. I've given Mr. Dutertre the exhibit number, it's open in front of the witness, and I think we will be able to move along more swiftly if Mr. Dutertre follows the cross-examination in the bundle because the photograph is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to just be clear about your answer. Your testimony is that the day you arrived, you saw with your own eyes two bodies, fully fleshed bodies, situated in the concrete section of the canal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just so that there is absolutely no doubt about it, if you would like to look behind tab 1 in the blue folder, there is a better photograph in colour, which is Exhibit D31, and bears a reference number U0094103. And so there is no doubt about it, your testimony is that you saw those two bodies in that photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just those two bodies. But upstream in that canal, a number of animals were seen who had died, so about 100 metres further upstream.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not concerned about the animals. It's a very important question that we need to try to clarify, whether those two bodies that you say that you saw in the concrete section of the canal were, in fact, there when you arrived in the canal area. And I want to make absolutely sure that you've had every opportunity to reconsider your testimony on this and that you're certain that you saw those two bodies in the concrete section of the canal when you arrived.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is it also your testimony that those two bodies were later on removed from the natural section of the canyon?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say that they were removed, they were floating in the water, and as the water went downstream, so did the bodies, and then they dropped down the waterfall into the natural part of the canal. It is in that sense that I use the word "removed." They moved. Later on, those bodies were probably in the group that we identified from the natural part of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to pause and take that in stages, please. The specific question I want to ask you to address with absolute clarity is whether your testimony to this Tribunal is that those two bodies were later removed by the police and the forensic teams from the canyon section and examined?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, there were two aspects of this that I'm going to suggest to you you are wrong about, and then we will look at it in a little more detail. First of all, the photograph that you're looking at there, which shows those two bodies in the canal, that photograph was taken on the 8th of September but I'm going to suggest to you that by the time you arrived, those two bodies had already gone and that there were no bodies in the concrete section of the canal by the time you arrived. That's my first suggestion. And the second suggestion is that neither of those two bodies appear in any of the forensic reports, autopsies or post mortems that you and your team conducted. That's the second part of the suggestion. Do you see?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. With respect to both parts of your suggestion, I would say the following. I did note those bodies. I don't know when they were photographed. And I don't know when those bodies reached the natural part of the canal. It is a fact that we couldn't mark them, and it is a fact that we couldn't link them to the bodies that we found in the canal. But in view of the fact that in the canal, a large number of bodies were found, it is realistic to assume that these two bodies were within the group of those bodies found downstream.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we are going to look at that in a little bit more detail in due course. The file that you have there, the blue file, contains the photographs of all of the bodies that were found downstream, in situ, and then again at Hotel Pastrik. It also contains the post mortem reports that you and your colleagues recorded, which of course include a record of the clothes that were found with each set of remains. And during the course of your examination, and if necessary with the benefit of some time overnight, I'm going to ask you to look at each of those photographs and reports and to confirm for the Tribunal that none of the bodies in those post mortem reports could possibly be either of the two bodies that we see in that photograph at the front. So I'm going to invite you in due course to make a comparison having regard to the sex, state of decomposition and clothing of the bodies that you and your team examined to determine whether it is even possible that any of -- either of those two bodies could be amongst the ones that you examined. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, before we get to that point, I wonder if I may just to come back to your testimony that you say you saw those two bodies in the canal. Could you look at your 92 ter statement, please? At paragraph 34, first of all. Now, that is in the files that you've got it is in the green file. I'm sure it's in many other places but it is in the green file behind tab 2 and if you could turn to paragraph 34, please? You there describe your arrival at the canal. And I'll read it in the English: "At first, we were shown by the police, the army and Judge Gojkovic the area of the concrete canal next to which we could see bodies. It was difficult to say the exact number of bodies as bodies and body parts were heaped together and/or partially buried. We were also informed that bodies had been seen floating in the canal. Different sources told us of this and we were given different numbers. I don't recall exactly who informed us of these bodies or the exact numbers." Pausing there for a moment, having refreshed your memory from that paragraph, Mr. Dunjic, is it still your evidence that you saw two bodies in the concrete section of the canal with your own eyes or not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I still claim that I did, but I must tell you that when we arrived and when we reached the canal, and when they told us what I refer to in this statement, the people who had come there a few days before that, that is, the investigating policemen and judge, I assume, they arrived there before we reached the canal on the 11th. They also saw bodies floating which the water was carrying along the concrete canal towards the natural part of the canal. And that is the information I'm conveying to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, in paragraph 34 of your witness statement, Mr. Dunjic, you are clear that you say that you saw bodies next to the canal by which you mean presumably bodies on the land; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you say that they were partially buried. You then go on to say that you were informed that bodies had been seen by others floating in the canal. Again, I'm asking you to reconsider whether, in fact, what you told the Trial Chamber in Milutinovic and what you repeated to this Trial Chamber when I started asking you questions is an observation which you are claiming to have seen, when in fact you are reporting something that somebody else has told you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said here refers to the bodies next to the canal, which I saw, and I participated in their examination. What I said in the other case, the Milutinovic case, I said with reference to events that took place in and around this canal. As for these two bodies, I saw them in that canal. The bodies that can be seen on this photograph. So these are three completely different things. One is what I saw; second is what was next to the canal; and third is the statement I made in the Milutinovic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, with the greatest of respect, they are all asking the same question which is did you see two bodies floating in the concrete section of the canal? What is the answer? When you arrived did you see two bodies floating in the concrete section of the canal? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why don't you mention them in paragraph 34, then? And why is it in paragraph 34 that you refer to other people telling you about them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't explain that, why it isn't stated in that paragraph. I was describing the whole event that I personally took part in. I can't remember each and every detail. When one reads something just now, it reminds me of many other details that I may not have mentioned or that I may not mention at this precise moment. So I really have no other explanation to give.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: These two bodies would have been very obvious to you, Mr. Dunjic, if you'd seen them on your arrival, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If he had seen these bodies, there would be an explanation for the reason it's not expressed in this way, in paragraph 34 of his 92 ter. This question has now been repeated for so many times I haven't counted them but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that it has not been completely answered. Professor Dunjic, you say, "I might have left out a lot of details." Now, in paragraph 34 you seem to give a very specific detail about bodies floating, that is, that you were informed that bodies had been seen floating in the canal, which language suggests that others had seen that. You said, "different sources told us of this." Now that very much suggests that when you gave that statement, that you had a precise recollection of your source of information about bodies floating in the canal, which is at least at first appearance quite different from what you told us today. That is that you had seen them yourself and not that you were informed that bodies had been seen, which suggests not by yourself. So that's what is bothering Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have fully understood after this discussion what the point is. This statement in paragraph 34 is given in general terms. A large number of people saw this and they passed on this information to me. But these two bodies is something that I saw myself. So I can't explain this in any other way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because in the canal itself, I beg your pardon, in the natural part of the canal that leads to the lake, we took out a large number of bodies which confirms the statements I had heard from others that many bodies had floated along the canal and that is what paragraph 34 refers to. As for these two bodies, I saw them. These are clear in my mind, these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In that case, I wonder if you could look at paragraph 36 of your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for this it would be helpful if the witness could be given the green file, oh, he has the green file.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you have a look at paragraph 36, the photograph that you're referring to there is behind tab 5 in the green file. So you'll need to look -- it may be easiest, Mr. Dunjic, if you take out the photograph in tab 5 and read it alongside your witness statement at paragraph 36, because you put certain markings on that photograph to indicate what happened and what you saw on your arrival.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes? You say on picture U0143054, I marked with a cross the letter -- and the letter A the place where we arrived on that day and we can see I think on annex 5 the letter A just to the right of the concrete section of the canal with an asterisk beside it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say, "I also marked with crosses and the letter B the places where bodies were lying close to the wall and after the waterfall." Do you see that? And there is a letter B on the photograph together with a line of -- together with a line of crosses which is a little difficult to see but if one looks closely one can see them on the colour copy, on the land at the side of the wall, as well as a further cross down in the canyon section in the water. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then you say, "I marked with an arrow and a letter D the direction where Dasinovac is located and I marked with an arrow and the letter E the direction of the economic farm." My question, Mr. Dunjic, is if you saw two bodies floating in the concrete section of the canal when you arrived at the scene, why on earth are there not crosses in the water there to indicate that that is where you saw two bodies?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mark where the other bodies were found either on this picture. But I can show you and mark where those two bodies were seen in this canal, because I thought that these are only the locations where groups of bodies were found and this one that was at the beginning of the natural part of the canal. However, the other places where bodies were found were not marked either, especially as this body that was seen, I don't know which of these two bodies were found later on in the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In paragraph 36, Mr. Dunjic, you're describing the scene as it appeared to you when you arrived, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not describing the scene. I'm describing the site, the location, where we worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let me move on, then, if I can, to the time of your arrival. When you came to this area for the first time and stood at that point marked A, were you with Mr. Aleksandric?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So we can take it then that he must have seen those two bodies floating in the canal as well, in the concrete section of the canal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can assume so but I don't know whether he saw them, whether he remembers that. I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you not discuss those two bodies and the need to remove them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we did. We did discuss that. But he was not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, I just want to be clear, if I can, with you, please, about when it was that you did first arrive at the canal, Mr. Dunjic. Could you look at your witness statement at paragraphs 25 and 27, please? In paragraph 25, you say, "I believe we arrived in Pec, Kosovo, on September the 10th around noon. It was ten years ago. I am not really sure." You see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then at paragraph 27, you say, "I believe, again I am not sure because it is a long time ago, that on the 10th of September, late in the morning, the MUP from Decan took us by car from Decan to the site of the canal near Lake Radonjic where the mortal remains, bodies and body parts, had been found by the MUP." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I just want to be clear about this. You didn't leave Belgrade until the morning of the day you arrived; is that correct? You went from Belgrade to this area, and then to the canal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I am able to recall regarding this detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we may be able to help you by reference to some of the documents, Mr. Dunjic. What would be the earliest time of day that you might have arrived there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know. I can't remember it now exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look in this green file behind tab 3, you will find -- and this is -- bear with me a moment. This is annex 3 to your 92 ter statement. You will find the request that is recorded as having been sent out by Judge Gojkovic on the 9th of September --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, perhaps for the previous photograph we looked at, that was 65 ter number 15 -- 1519, and the one you're now looking at is -- yes, annex 3 to the Rule 92 ter statement but it seems not to have or -- a 65 ter number, whereas the other annex which was annex 5 to it, did have a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think that it's been marked as 1D53-0207.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is the request that was sent out to your facility in Belgrade on the 9th of September, Mr. Dunjic, and behind tab 4 is the response from Professor Veljkovic on the 10th of September do you see that? And that would be annex 4 to your statement, document 1D53/0209. Do you see those two documents?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now I want to suggest to that you it was not until the 11th that you and your colleagues travelled to the canal.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't know if you heard my question correctly. I want to suggest to you that it was not until the 11th of September that you and your colleagues travelled to the canal.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 11th. That's why I said that I could not remember the exact date, whether it was on the 10th or the 11th. There is the record, and the minutes of our presence and of what we did, that is dated the 11th of September. I said immediately that after all this time I'm unable to tell you whether this was on the 10th or the 11th but on the 11th we were there on the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, there may still be some lack of clarity in the answer that you have given. Do you accept now having looked at those documents that it was not until the 11th that you and Mr. Aleksandric first went to the canal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And I think, if we look - just bear with me for one moment - behind tab 7 in the green file, you'll find a statement that you made in March and April 2006, and at paragraph 19 of that statement, Mr. Dunjic, you say, in terms, that the 11th of September was the first day of your arrival at the site. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I take it that you're not going to tender that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The statement, no. I'm simply inviting the witness to confirm now that his 92 ter statement is in error and that the date of arrival was the 11th and not the 10th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then of course it would be -- it would have been better always to first of all identify the document by number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then to read the portion of the statement you seek confirmation of so that at least it's clear on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Shall I do that now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it was U0094903, paragraph 19 of this statement, which reads, "On the 11th of September 1998, the first day of our arrival at the site, we started our activities by ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it is in fact Defence document 1D07-0561 for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dunjic, we've heard testimony from others who attended the scene, and it is, I'm going to suggest to you, perfectly clear that by the 11th there were no bodies in the concrete section of the canal. They had gone. If you'd like just for a moment, please, to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the witness lifted his shoulders, which does not appear on the transcript. He seems to not agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And he now confirms this by nodding.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon, Your Honour. I cannot comment on this comment. This was something that was stated by some witnesses, if I understood it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you just bear with me for a moment, if you could look -- I wonder if the witness could just be shown the yellow binder. And I'd like if you -- the witness to be shown tab 14, please, paragraphs 85 and 86.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, that seems to be the 92 ter statement of Zarko Bajcetic which has no P number yet. It has an exhibit -- so therefore would you please try to find that and then later for the record --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's P377.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Paragraphs 85 and 86. Commenting on the video recordings which I shall show you after our first break, Mr. Dunjic, reads as follows: "With respect to the recordings made of the site at the canal and the canyon, it has to be stressed that the two bodies which can be seen on the video footage recorded on the 8th of September cannot be seen anymore on the video footage made on the 9th and the 10th. One of the bodies is wearing a red shirt and the second one is wearing a blue one. "The reason why those two bodies cannot be seen anymore on these dates because heavy rain on the 8th of September caused the water to sweep both bodies downstream towards the lake. I know this based on what the cameraman told me and because the recording was different than what we saw on the 10th of September. Cameraman told me that the bodies were present on the 8th but they were not present on the 10th." You see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you were reading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see whether everything has been -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. That witness has testified orally before the Tribunal that from his own observations, he can be certain that by the time he arrived at the canal scene at 11.00 on the 10th those two bodies were not there, indeed there were no bodies in the concrete section of the canal, Mr. Dunjic. So I'm going to ask you to reconsider. What is the position? Do you think you may be wrong in the testimony you've given?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, after, regarding those two bodies I am convinced that I saw them, and that's all I can tell you. That's all I know. I can see those photographs still in my mind's eye.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know how to explain this in any other way. I have the picture of those two bodies in my mind's eye. I can see them. After this much time, after ten years, now you bring what I said into doubt and you also make me doubt whether I actually saw them or not, but I remember those photographs or rather not the photographs but the images that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think I've given you about four opportunities up until now, Mr. Dunjic, to tell us if you're not sure about this and until this point, up until now, you've told us on each occasion that you are sure. Is it the position now that you are no longer sure that you saw them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know how to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can allow that but I have this vivid image of what I saw. It is possible that I linked it in temporal terms with the photographs but I also saw the bodies. I really can't explain what happened here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, I wonder whether that would be a convenient moment to take a short break because I have to organise a short passage of video to be played to the witness and it is difficult for me to do that, there is a technical problem and I wonder if we might do that in the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, Mr. Emmerson, I did not watch the clock very carefully. We are already far beyond the time when we should have had the break, with apologies to the interpreters and the technicians. We will have a break until 25 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the Chamber would like to turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar. The witness can be brought in again. I do understand that counsel for Mr. Balaj has not reached any agreement on the latest motion and therefore is expected to file -- if he wants to further respond to the Prosecution's response, to do that by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Professor Dunjic, we had to urgently deal with a procedural matter totally unrelated to your testimony. Therefore we had to ask you to wait a couple of minutes outside. Thank you for your understanding. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to play you now a short section of videotape that was recorded as having been taken in -- of the concrete section of the canal at 10.48 a.m. on the morning of the 10th of September. Don't be misled by the time shown on the screen because the evidence is that that is 12 hours ahead. So the time of this piece of footage is 10.48 a.m. on the 10th and for the record it is video V000-7064, Exhibit P72, at 10.48. And on the counter it should say 20:10, that is 20 minutes, ten seconds. It's a very short piece of footage. Could we see that now, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pausing there, thank you. Could we just run that one more time, please? Sorry, we -- do you have it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Professor Dunjic, do you see a video image on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please assist the witness? I think maybe e-court would be better. Can I ask whether all parties have the same difficulty on the e-court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact -- I think we have now the right starting moment again. It earlier looked like as if we were in a disco. Everyone is invited to look at the video channel. Madam Usher, therefore, for the witness as well. I think we have on the video channel now the starting image of what you would like to show. Is that correct, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you have an image of the canal on your screen now, Mr. Dunjic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a little dark in the video channel but I think if you look on the right-hand side you can confirm that there is no sign of any remains floating in the concrete section of the canal that is shown in that piece of video. Do you see that? Perhaps we should just play it for you now very briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this clip, one cannot see the bodies. But if you can wind it back to the beginning, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here at the beginning, just behind the date and the year, and in front of the letters p.m., one gets the impression that there are bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you just take the photograph in the blue file, please, behind tab 1, Mr. Dunjic? You can see the two objects that are floating in the water. Whether they are debris or wood or other objects, we can see them in the centre of the channel.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the middle of the canal, of the fourth cascade. And the two bodies are laterally on the photograph, close to the edge of the concrete wall of the canal. This is on the photograph. But I don't see them here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We are finished with the video for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I don't know whether if you're done with that video but could we have the first image again on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It will just play from here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The place where you locate the bodies on the photograph, is that portion of the canal in view of the Defence visible on the first image of this video footage? Because if I -- I look at it, then I see a horizontal and I would like to know that I'm speaking therefore I should -- I would like to have the image shown. I'll wait until it's there. Yes, there we are again. We see a first horizontal part closest to the natural part. Then we see a second level, horizontal further up. Then we see the third level further up. As far as I understand, and comparing the images also of the walls, as a matter of fact, that only a very, very small portion, well, let's say the first one or two metres on the right-hand side of the wall is visible of that level where, on the photograph, the bodies are located.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I take Your Honour's point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this, Mr. Dunjic? You have indicated in your witness statement at paragraph 75 that the rain began a few days after you arrived at the scene; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So can we take it, then, that it was possible to recover remains for the first few days following your arrival?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th and on the 12th, where we -- when we were at the scene, it was very warm and it was possible to pull out the bodies. We made a break. I think it was until the 15th of September, because of the heavy rains. And then we resumed work later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So again so that we are clear, between the 13th and the 14th, you say there was no recovery operation going on because the rain was so heavy; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then on the 15th, you say, in paragraph 76 in your statement, that the recovery operation began again in the afternoon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But most of the remains that you examined and your team examined were recovered on the 11th and the 12th, were they not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the diver's team was there by the 12th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I think it was on the 12th. I mean, one can find this in writing. There is a record of it somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll look at that in a moment. If the position is that it was perfectly possible to recover bodies on the 11th and the 12th, that the weather was warm and that there was no obstruction, can you think of any reason why, if those two bodies had been in the canal, in the concrete section of the canal when you first arrived on the 11th, they wouldn't have been recovered during those first two days?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honours, I have been thinking during the break about this issue that we have been discussing, and I really am in a great dilemma as a witness. In my mind, I have living impressions of having seen this and it is my impression that those pictures of those two bodies in the canal, as I saw them, and having seen all these documents and everything else, and the statement of the witness who made the video recording, seem to indicate that on the 10th, the bodies already were not in the canal. But those pictures remain in my mind and I am now in a human dilemma as a physician: Is this something that I really saw or is it the photographs that I saw? I am really in a dilemma. I do not wish to cause any doubts as a witness. I'm expressing my human, personal dilemma about this. However, in my mind is impressed the picture of those corpses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, perhaps you can try to cut matters short. The Chamber does understand that you have difficulties to reconcile a vivid visual impression of these bodies which you linked to personally having seen them, with a rational way of reconciling this impression with other information that reached you by now that is testimony from other witnesses, other information, et cetera. Is that correctly understood? I think dilemmas, Mr. Emmerson, are characterised by not being immediately resolved. I think we could proceed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we now look, please, in the green file, behind tab number 1, which contains, in English, a record of a meeting that you had with Mr. Dutertre on the 3rd of July of this year when you were asked questions about those two bodies shown in the photograph that I have taken you to in the blue volume, that is to say photograph D31? Now, I'm not sure how good your English is, Mr. Dunjic. You should be looking behind tab number 1. I think you're looking behind tab 2. You've got the right file but previous tab, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's just one page, Professor Dunjic, tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in that note -- can I be clear, do you read English?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let me just take you through it briefly, if I can. You were shown by Mr. Dutertre the transcript of your evidence in the Milutinovic case and the photograph that you've just looked at and you repeat there, in the first two bullet points, that you thought at least that you'd seen those two bodies at the time, and you say, in the second bullet point, "Those bodies later turned up in the earthen part of the canal. This was due to the heavy rain pushing bodies down the canal. We saw these two floating bodies when we first arrived and started work." And in the fourth bullet point, "The two floating bodies were recovered later on. I guess these two bodies were the bodies later recovered in the earthen part of the canal. These were the bodies of two males. They could (emphasise could) be R20 or R21. In other words, anyone from R20 onwards found in the natural part of the canal." Do you see that? Yes? Now, again, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't think the transcript picked up the witness's response.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've understood that passage, have you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And again I'm going to give you the opportunity to clarify whether you're certain of your recollection, Mr. Dunjic. You said to the Prosecution that those two bodies were recovered in the earthen part of the canal. Is that your testimony to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You have a recollection of that, do you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Examining the bodies and the post mortem of R-20 and R-21, the bodies that were found in the canal, and they were males, or, rather, persons that could correspond to those on the photographs, that is what I had in mind. That it is possible that those were the two persons from the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, what you told us earlier on in your testimony this afternoon and what you told Mr. Dutertre in the course of the meeting that you had, and indeed the evidence that you gave in the Milutinovic trial, was not that it was possible that those two bodies had been recovered but that they had recovered and in this instance that it was possible that they were R-20 and R-21. The question I'm asking you to be absolutely clear is do you -- are you in a position to say to this Tribunal that the two bodies you see in that photograph were in fact recovered from the canyon or not? Whichever bodies which you say they might have been, are you in a position to tell the Tribunal that those two bodies were in fact recovered from the canyon at any point and examined by your team?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to start from the following in my answer: And that is that the team that had searched the natural part of the canal, the canyon, leading towards the Radonjic lake, dragged out all the bodies that they found and that according to certain anthropometric characteristics, which we were able to note on this photograph, it is possible that they correspond to R-20 and R-21. This is not absolutely certain. This is just a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let's just test that with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, page 22, line 7 of today's testimony already makes it clear that we are talking about, where the witness said, "But in view of the fact that in the canal, a large number of bodies were found, it is realistic to assume that these two bodies were within the group of those bodies found downstream." Which already makes clear that it has not, at least in view of the expert's opinion, it has not been solidly been established that they were. So whether it would then be, if you would be able to positively identify R-20 or R-21 as the two bodies floating in the canal on the picture, then of course we would not ever have accepted -- ever have expected the witness to say this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, detailed information about the bodies floating is missing. And therefore, I mean, you see a bit, but it's all rather vague information, which I would say almost automatically disenables an expert to compare the bodies found and the bodies shown on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you want to bear with me for a moment because it's going to be our submission that that is not the case, that it's perfectly possible to make a comparison and I seek if I may through some questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the comparison would be negative. Okay, please proceed. But I didn't want to -- I think you were revisiting a matter which to some extent already had been dealt with by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think at page 44, line 11 the witness indicated, and there is a word missing from the transcript, that it was possible to compare certain anthropomorphic characteristics from the photograph to see whether there was a correspondence. And I wanted Mr. Dunjic, just to ask you about the question of comparing anthropomorphic characteristics on the photograph. Just to take an example if you could turn, please, to tab 2 and to tab 3 in the bundle, you will see closer photographs of those two sets of remains. Do you see those? If you turn to tabs 2 and 3, it might be easier to manage the papers on your desk, Mr. Dunjic, if you just had that blue file and only that blue file in front of you because I think otherwise things are going to get a bit confusing. In the proofing note that we just looked at, you say record that both of the bodies that you can see in the canal are male. On what basis did you reach that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of these photographs, which are relatively clear, one can see that these are adults. One person is wearing trousers and the body structure would correspond to a male. The other person, though it is hard to see this, according to its build, could also be a male. But I must draw your attention that what looks like the colour red, that is more likely part of the body than part of the clothing. This applies to both bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. If we can just focus, please, then, for a moment on the photograph that is behind tab number 2, which, for the record, is Exhibit D43, we can agree, I imagine, Mr. Dunjic, that the adult in that photograph is wearing a pair of white trousers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it looks like, though one trouser leg is darker in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. They are clearly light-coloured trousers, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the bodies appear fully fleshed, do they not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't assert that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You can presumably make an observation in that regard about the torso of the body behind tab 3. That is D44. Because we can see that exposed, can we not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is naked. It seems that some of the clothes had been pulled over the head and as for the rest of the clothing, the lower body seems to be clothed up to the mid-thigh and we can see part of the body here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you confirm for me, Mr. Dunjic, that we are looking there at what appears to be the buttocks of a fully-fleshed torso?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With most of the tissue intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want, if I may, with you, please, to focus on the body that's shown behind tab 2, that is to say photograph D43, and with that body in mind, I want to look with you at the remaining sets of remains that were recovered lower in the canal. And they are all in that file for you. If you turn just beyond tab 4 you will see that there was a gap in the numbering and they begin at 18. And that is so that you're in a position to remind yourself of the numbers, because the numbers that run from 18 through to 35 are the R numbers that were assigned to each set of remains. If you look behind tab 18, as an example, you will see that there are photographs, where they are available, of the remains in situ then post mortem photographs followed by photographs of clothing where they are available - they are not in this instance because there were no clothes - followed by the post mortem report in Serbian, B/C/S, followed by the English translation of that report. And we can take this at a reasonable pace, Mr. Dunjic. We can exclude R-18, can't we, because that was the partly burned body of a woman; is that right? So that the body that we are looking for, the man wearing white trousers, cannot be R-18, can it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, R-18 was a female body.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you agree that we can exclude R-18 from the list of possible candidates?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We could exclude it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: R-18-1 was a partial skull which was later found to belong to the same body as R-32?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that was also the body of a woman without clothes, was it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm sorry for interrupting. When we earlier talked about comparisons, I was talking about positive identification, and I said comparison wouldn't make sense if you are missing quite a lot of details on the bodies which just appear in the photograph. Now, comparing, that's at least how I understand it now, you'd like to compare to see when differences, clear differences, are found then you could come to a negative opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we go through all of these pictures, would it not be better to invite the witness to look at those portions of the material you provided to him, to ask him whether, if he looked at it this evening, whether there is any of these data which would not show such differences that it would allow for a negative identification and that we would focus exclusively on those pictures, of those bodies found, and those post mortems, where the witness considers that it could not be excluded?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Professor Dunjic, do you understand what I'm seeking to do, in order to save time? You may have noticed that already, where Mr. Emmerson took you to the body under number 18, that he said, well, on the basis of photographs, post mortem, et cetera, et cetera, this is not a male body, this is a female body, it's not fully fleshed, et cetera, so therefore it could that the differences would not allow even for the possibility that the bodies, the two bodies, shown floating in the concrete part, could be identical to the one under number 18. Now, what the Chamber would like you to do, and I already apologise perhaps for spoiling your evening, to go in this blue binder through all the numbered tabs and see whether there is any of these bodies which -- for which you would find no such distinction between what you established in relation to the two bodies on the photograph floating in the river, that you would still consider it possible that these photographs of these bodies found further down in the canal, could be the bodies shown in the photographs. Then, Mr. Emmerson tomorrow would perhaps take you to those bodies you considered possibly to be the same as the two bodies floating in the canal in the photograph, and then he might go into more detail as far as that is concerned. So therefore, you exclude all the non-male -- well, or those where -- you understand what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In order to assist that task, Mr. Dunjic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you give the details to specifically pay attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask to you have regard to the state of decomposition of the remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think as a matter of fact the witness should be allowed now to write down what the specific points of reference are that you would like him to look at. I take it gender?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Gender, state of decomposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could go slowly so Professor Dunjic could write it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And clothing as recorded either in the photographs of the clothing at Hotel Pastrik or in the post mortem reports which set out the clothing in which the remains were found. And so, for example, I'm going to suggest to that you there isn't a single body amongst the bodies numbered R-18 to R-35, which could have been wearing -- have been a male wearing white trousers, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or light-coloured trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Or light-coloured trousers. And you have fairly detailed records of clothing and of the degree of decomposition in the remains. And so, for example, with R-20, which is one of the ones you have mentioned, it may be helpful for you to know that Mr. Aleksandric has testified that based on the state of saponification, the body R-20 must have been lodged in the position in which it was found for several weeks. That is transcript T6794. So if you could pay attention to those features overnight and perhaps tomorrow tell us which of the bodies you say are candidates for being either of those two bodies, and I'm sorry to add to your burdens but there is a third body which appears to have gone missing from the post mortem reports, and that is behind tabs 4A and B, photographs taken on the 8th of September. There is a body shown floating in the natural section of the canyon which also does not seem to correspond with any of the post mortem reports. So could I ask you to include that body, as far as you're able to, in the comparisons that you're being invited to conduct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Professor Dunjic, perhaps we provide you with this portion of the transcript, since you read English. I take it that you're mastering the English language sufficiently to have this for your guidance for your homework this evening. And I again apologise but it's raining anyhow so --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll come back then if I may to that aspect of your evidence tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you now give the usher back the blue file and take the green file again? And obviously, Professor Dunjic will need to have the blue file to take away with him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will take care at the end of today's hearing that the blue file would be provided to Professor Dunjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn to tab 8, please, in the green file? I just want to ask you about some other apparent anomalies. This is a witness statement of Goran Jovovic, who is recorded as a crime scene technician, and this is Defence document 1D53-0211, and you have it both in English at 8A and in Serbian or B/C/S at 8B. I'm sorry, I apologise, the original is in English and the translation is in Albanian so if we could work from the English version, please, paragraph 11, I just want to go through two paragraphs with you, it reads as follows and I'll read it slowly: "We started working immediately. Together with the forensic experts and some helpers from the local burial company, we started to exhume the bodies there. My task was to fix and label all the evidence at the scene. Besides the bodies also other evidence was found. One blanket for a baby was discovered next to the bodies. When the blanket was opened, bones of a very small human being were found. The bones were covered by a small baby sweater with buttons on it, also a pacifier and pampers were found in this blanket." Then if you could pick it up please in paragraph 33 in this statement, it reads as follows: "I remember also that at the first day of my presence at the Canal, the journalist, Miroslav Lazanski appeared at the crime scene. When he was informed about the findings of the remains of a baby at the spot, he requested me to give him the photographs of it. After getting the authorisation from my superior" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Sorry, from which paragraph are you reading?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "After getting the authorisation from my superiors I gave him a few photographs about the remains of the baby." Mr. Dunjic, it's not true, is it, that the bones of any baby or infant were recovered and examined by your team?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right but I can explain. A pacifier was found at the scene and that led us to believe that there was a baby or an infant there. But none of the bodies, none of the bones found there at the canal, by the canal, belonged to a baby or an infant. Now, the dilemma remained where the pacifier had come from and now I have to testify and say that we asked questions when people came to identify the remains, we asked whether anyone had been there with a baby or an infant, be they male or female, and we were told that two of the Albanian men who had been -- who had been on their way to Prizren by bus and they had been arrested, that one of them had gone there to get some stuff for a baby. He had been taken off the bus. If I am not mistaken, Olga Gashi testified to that effect and he had been taken off the bus because the previous day, when the bus had been stopped, the bus that he had been on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to, if I may, interrupt the witness at this point because there have been certain rulings in respect of this aspect of the testimony and in order to explore the answer that the witness has given which is inconsistent with the record in his original witness statement, it would be necessary to go behind that part of the ruling and agreement which has been reached between the parties in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The question I was asking you, Mr. Dunjic is a relatively simple one which is that where Mr. Jovovic has recorded the fact that the bones of a very small human being were found, that isn't correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. I cannot agree to that because we, as experts, did not determine that. And he is a layperson, after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you turn to paragraph 18 of his witness statement, please? I just want to ask you for some clarifications about this. He says at paragraph 18, and I'll read it slowly, "At the beginning of the natural part of the canal, one car was found in the water. In the trunk of this car, an Opel Kadett, the body of a woman who later turned out to be Ilira Frrokaj was found. I remember that it was the body which was labelled number 18 during the course of the exhumation. The trunk was opened by me and (redacted). After succeeding to open it we found a completely naked woman therein. There were no clothes in the trunk either." Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pausing there for a moment before I ask you questions about it, would you turn behind tab 9 to the statement of (redacted), the man who is there referred to? And this is Defence 1D07-0238, and would you turn please to paragraph 24 in that statement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Where is it? Where is his statement? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab 9.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you have it again in English first and then in Albanian. And I'm looking at paragraph 24 in the English version, the last four lines of the paragraph where this witness is recorded as having said, "In the canyon, I saw a red Opel Kadett car on its roof. Close to the car there were two bodies, a male and a female. The female and male were later identified. They were a married Catholic Albanian couple who probably were thrown into the canyon with the car." And at paragraph 25 he continues, "After the bodies were identified, the family was brought to the scene to view the red Opel Kadett car. They identified the car as belonging to the couple. These bodies were partly burned." Do you see that passage? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
